newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals mostly steady, Comex closed.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals mostly steady, Comex closed.

text.p: Gold prices were slightly easier on Monday afternoon, but the precious metals markets were quiet due to U.S. markets being closed for the Labour Day holiday.
Bullion fixed at $386.55 an ounce, compared to $386.90 in the morning and a London close of $386.10/$386.60.
The trading range was very tight with bids quoted so far between $387.10 and $386.35 an ounce.
Gold had bounced late on Friday following a break higher by silver. Dealers had attributed silver's strength to a surge in copper, which continued its rally early on Monday.
But dealers expected little action in gold with Comex shut.
Overnight, gold prices in the Tokyo market had plunged due to active selling by some Japanese trade houses overnight.
But traders there said the falls would likely be shortlived, because they were due to technical factors and not related to physical selling.
The precious metals markets are expected to pick up steam as soon as Tuesday as the seasonal lull winds down and technical factors reach a cusp, dealers said.
"Tomorrow will be very important since technically both gold and silver are at a crossroads and also the big fund managers will be returning," a dealer said.
One technical analyst said gold's support around $386 would hold, allowing gold to make a break higher in the near term and surmount the tough $388 resistance level.
Elliot Wave International, however, said in a commentary that gold could decline towards $384.70-$383.90 this week, with the longer term prospect unclear.
Silver was up three cents from Friday's London close at $5.18/$5.20, but trading in a very tight range all day.
Platinum was up $0.60 at $395.50/$396.50, while palladium was up $0.50 at $125.50/$126.50.
